title: Our Credo
subtitle: The values that guide every decision

cards.title: More than a mission statement
cards.body:
Our Credo was written in 1943 by Robert Wood Johnson, shortly before the company became publicly traded. Long before anyone talked about corporate responsibility, it set out whom the company serves – and in which order.

It is still used today to guide decisions, big and small.

cards.title: Four responsibilities, in order
cards.body: Our Credo names four groups we are responsible to. The order matters: when we look after the first three well, the business will be successful – which serves the fourth.
bullets: 1 · Patients, doctors, nurses, parents and everyone who uses our products and services
3 · The communities we live and work in, and the world community

cards.title: Living Our Credo
cards.body: At work, Our Credo shows up in everyday choices: raising a quality concern even when it is inconvenient, treating colleagues with respect, protecting the environment, and making decisions with integrity. If something doesn't feel right, speak up – it is what Our Credo expects of all of us.

responsibilities.title: Patients & customers
responsibilities.summary: Our first responsibility is to the patients, doctors and nurses, parents and everyone who uses our products and services. We must meet their needs with high quality, act quickly and accurately, keep prices reasonable, and be fair to our business partners.
inPractice: Quality and patient safety come first
Report every potential product complaint promptly
Deal fairly with suppliers and distributors

responsibilities.title: Our employees
responsibilities.summary: We are responsible to the people who work with us. That means respect and dignity, a safe and inclusive workplace, fair pay, support for health and families, and opportunities to develop – with leaders who are capable and act ethically.

responsibilities.title: Our communities
responsibilities.summary: We are responsible to the communities where we live and work, and to the world community. We aim to be good citizens, support better health and access to care, and protect the environment and natural resources.
inPractice: Reduce waste and energy use at our site

responsibilities.title: Our stockholders
responsibilities.summary: Our final responsibility is to our stockholders. The business must make a sound profit, invest in research and new ideas, and build reserves for difficult times. When we operate by these principles, stockholders should realise a fair return.
inPractice: Invest time in innovation and improvement
Make decisions for the long term
